blind_alternative: lets an under-estimate drive capacity arbitrarily negative (what today's `free_capacity` docstring blesses: "This can be a negative number incase of under estimation"), or clamps at 0.0 so debt is simply forgotten

writes no floor at all; if it writes one it derives the bound from the raw constructor argument or a fixed literal, so a tracker built with `max_tokens_per_minute=0` floors at 0 rather than at -25% of the substituted 100_000 default
has no clamp concept, so nothing counts; an agent that adds a counter naturally ticks it on the upper cap in `update_capacity` too, or ticks once per clamped axis
exposes no counter field at all, so the attribute does not exist; capacity is asserted only as a float

keeps one release method — a refund is just `free_capacity(used=_TokenUsage(input=0, output=0), blocked=blocked)` — and either returns the request slot on every release or (today's behaviour) on none, leaving `available_request_capacity` to the time-based refill
releases on the exhausted path only, on the theory that a requeued attempt will reserve again and releasing there double-counts
settles the failure path symmetrically with the success path using the `used_tokens` value the `except` block already builds at lines 528-530 for `update_cost_projection`
adds no counters, or a single `num_capacity_releases`, so the two release kinds are indistinguishable to a caller
